mainEntity.name: How long do same-day partial dentures last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Same-day partial dentures are generally considered a temporary or transitional solution. They are designed to be worn during the healing period following extraction, which typically lasts several months. During this time, changes in the gum and bone shape mean the denture may need relining or adjusting. Once healing is complete, your dentist will usually recommend a definitive partial denture — crafted to fit the fully healed mouth — or discuss alternative long-term replacement options. The lifespan of the immediate denture itself depends on the materials used, how well it is cared for, and the extent of tissue changes during healing.

Some degree of discomfort is normal in the first few days, particularly as the extraction sites heal. The gums may feel sore, and the denture may create pressure points that need adjustment. Most patients find that discomfort improves significantly within the first week or two. Your dentist will schedule follow-up appointments to address any areas of irritation and adjust the fit as needed. If discomfort persists or worsens, it is important to contact your dental practice rather than attempting to modify the denture yourself, as this can cause further problems.

mainEntity.name: Can I eat normally with immediate partial dentures?

acceptedAnswer.text: Eating will feel different initially, and most dentists recommend starting with soft foods such as soups, scrambled eggs, mashed vegetables, and yoghurt. As you become more accustomed to the denture and the extraction sites heal, you can gradually reintroduce firmer foods. It is advisable to chew evenly on both sides to help keep the denture stable. Very hard, sticky, or chewy foods should be approached with caution. Over time, most patients regain a good level of eating function, though some dietary adjustments may remain advisable depending on the type and extent of the denture.

mainEntity.name: How much do same-day partial dentures cost in London?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost of immediate partial dentures in London varies depending on several factors, including the number of teeth being replaced, the materials used, the complexity of the case, and whether additional treatments such as extractions are included. It is important to obtain a detailed treatment plan and cost breakdown during your initial consultation. Many practices offer payment plans to help spread the cost. Rather than choosing a provider based on price alone, consider the quality of the consultation, the aftercare provided, and whether the practice discusses all suitable treatment alternatives with you.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to remove my same-day denture at night?

acceptedAnswer.text: For the first 24 hours after fitting, your dentist may advise keeping the denture in place — including overnight — to help protect the extraction sites and manage swelling. After this initial period, it is generally recommended to remove the denture at night to give your gums a chance to rest. Leaving a denture in continuously can reduce blood circulation to the underlying tissues and increase the risk of fungal infections such as denture stomatitis. Cleaning the denture and your mouth thoroughly before bed and again in the morning supports good oral health throughout the healing period.

mainEntity.name: Will people notice I am wearing a partial denture?

acceptedAnswer.text: Modern partial dentures are designed to blend as naturally as possible with your remaining teeth. Tooth-coloured clasps and carefully matched acrylic materials help create a discreet appearance. However, the cosmetic result depends on the type of denture, the materials chosen, and the individual clinical situation. Your dentist will discuss the aesthetic options available during your consultation. Many patients find that their immediate partial denture provides a very acceptable appearance, particularly for front teeth, which is often the primary reason patients request same-day provision in the first place.
